name: Tournament
description: Four contenders propose independent approaches to the same brief, two pairwise judges each pick a winner and carry its artifact forward, and one final judge compares the two survivors to crown a single champion.

charter.mission: Choose the best of several approaches by comparing them in pairs, so every judgment is between two things a judge can hold side by side, rather than a ranking of four things nobody compared directly.
conventions: A judge decides between the two artifacts in front of it on the brief's terms. It does not invent a third approach, and it does not send work back — there is nobody to send it to.
A pairwise judge carries the winning artifact forward verbatim. The final judge cannot reach past its own inputs to fetch it.
nonGoals: Merging two approaches into a hybrid. The bracket picks one; a hybrid is a new contender for a new run.
Producing the implementation. Every context here is read-only: the tournament chooses an approach, and building it is separate work.

invariants.statement: No contender reads another contender's proposal. Four independent attempts at one brief is what makes the comparison meaningful.

Each pairwise judge banks the winning artifact's CONTENT, not only the winner's id. Upstream inputs reach a context's direct predecessors only, so by the final round the contenders are two hops away and unreadable — an unforwarded artifact is one the final judge can never see.
The final round names exactly one champion and the artifact behind it, so the decision is legible without replaying the bracket.

sourcesOfTruth.label: Tournament brief
sourcesOfTruth.description: The problem every contender proposes against and the tradeoff axes every judge decides on: what has to be true of a good approach, and what is being traded against what.

sourcesOfTruth.label: Repository engineering contract
sourcesOfTruth.description: The engineering contract any winning approach would have to be implementable under — typing, testing, and architecture boundaries.

tasks.title: Propose an approach
tasks.instructions:
Read the tournament brief named as rank 1 in the charter.

Propose ONE approach to it. Make it concrete enough that a reader could implement from your proposal without asking you a follow-up question: name the mechanism, where it lives, and what changes. A direction of travel is not a proposal.

State what your approach trades away as well as what it buys. A judge that has to discover your tradeoff for itself will assume the worst one.

You are read-only. You have no worktree and you will make no commit, so your captured output is your entire delivery — in particular, `artifact` is the thing judges will compare, so it must stand on its own. You cannot see the other contenders, and that is deliberate: four independent attempts are what make the comparison worth running.

tasks.title: Judge A against B and carry the winner forward
tasks.instructions:
The two proposals you are judging are in the "Inputs from upstream" section of this prompt, as validated structured output. Read `artifact` for each — that is the proposal itself, not a summary of it.

Decide between them on the brief's tradeoff axes. Compare; do not re-describe. If both are viable, say what the deciding axis was, and if one is disqualified rather than merely beaten, say that too.

Then carry the winner forward. Your captured `winningArtifact` must contain the winning proposal's FULL content, copied verbatim from its `artifact` field — not a summary, not a citation, and not the winner's id again. The final judge sees only its direct predecessors, which are the two semifinals; the contenders are two hops away and completely invisible to it. An artifact you do not copy into `winningArtifact` is one the final judge can never read, and it will be judging a name.

You are read-only. You have no worktree and you will make no commit. Do not propose an approach of your own.

tasks.title: Crown the champion
tasks.instructions:
The two semifinal verdicts are in the "Inputs from upstream" section of this prompt. Each carries a `winningArtifact` — the full proposal that won its half of the bracket. Those two artifacts are everything you can see: the four original contenders are two hops upstream and are not available to you.

Compare the two artifacts on the brief's tradeoff axes and choose exactly one champion. Do not defer to the semifinal judges' rationales — they each compared a different pair, and neither of them has seen what you are seeing.

Copy the champion's full content into `championArtifact` so the decision is readable without replaying the bracket, and name its originating contender in `championContextId`.

You are read-only. You have no worktree and you will make no commit. Complete this task with a summary naming the champion and the axis that decided it.
